records.basis: Mapping HOLD: `DocumentActivator(documents)` accepts a mapping of names to document dictionaries and promises independent stored data. It calls `deepcopy(documents)` directly. A `types.MappingProxyType({'doc': {'sections': ['x']}})` is an ordinary read-only Mapping with ordinary copyable contents; direct deepcopy is predicted to raise TypeError. No dict-only or deepcopy-compatible-wrapper restriction is specified. Snapshotting the mapping contents is feasible. Original tests use dict only; their successful nested copies do not settle wrapper breadth.

Mapping/API HOLD: `compile_catalog(batches, schemes)` constrains the inner record `name` to nonempty string, but does not restrict batch mapping keys to strings. The reference adds `isinstance(batch_name, str)` and rejects `{1: [('x', b'a')]}` with TypeError, even though the mapping and record satisfy the stated rules. Expected shape for scheme `sample2` is `{1: {'sample2': {'x': (97,)}}}`. Tests only use string batch keys. Freeze the batch-key restriction explicitly in recovery or preserve valid mapping keys; do not infer it from the identifier `batch_name`.

Mapping HOLD: `find_notices` expressly accepts notice mappings. A matching `MappingProxyType` containing required string fields and `published=True` passes structural validation, then reaches `deepcopy(notice)` and is predicted to fail with TypeError. No noncopyable descendants are needed. Normalize the mapping container before copying, or explicitly restrict the contract in recovery. Existing scalar-validation test cases also have extra list wrappers; that coverage weakness remains separate, not the basis for this Mapping hold.

Mapping HOLD: `stage_module` describes `cache` and `available` as mappings, preserves their ownership and returns a detached cache that can receive downloaded content. It calls `deepcopy(cache)` without normalizing the mapping. Even an empty `MappingProxyType({})` on the no-match path is predicted to fail; the download path also assumes the copied mapping is mutable. Tests exercise plain dicts only. The contract does not say mutable-input-cache or deepcopy-compatible concrete wrapper.

`pageDirectory` reconstructs required id/label explicitly and is sound for this scope. However `omitDirectoryEntry` validates the same public records through ordinary property access, then spreads retained records. A valid retained record with non-enumerable id/label is returned without those required fields. The public DirectoryEntry contract does not restrict required fields to enumerable own properties. Original tests only omit plain literal entries and therefore miss the loss.

`add` accepts primitive owner/title/priority arguments, validates them and creates the complete internal Bookmark literal. All later spreads operate on that internally created object, not a caller-supplied record with hidden/inherited required fields. Returned records are detached. Original tests exercise mutations of add/list results and confirm isolation; no requirement to support mutation of private storage is added.

All three Feature fields are read directly, trimmed and assigned explicitly into a new literal. Non-enumerable or inherited required values are preserved as sanitized own fields. Tests check every trimmed field, duplicate normalized keys, order and two-way mutation isolation. The earlier sparse-array question is separate and is not a property-copy failure.

Constructor input is strings, not public StoredMessage objects. `send` creates an internal literal containing sequence/text; reads spread those literals. Snapshot constructs path/messages explicitly. Original tests check independent arrays/messages and altered sequence/text results. No caller-controlled property descriptor can enter stored message fields through the specified API.

Performance constructor and draft addition reconstruct required fields explicitly, but update uses `{...current, ...patch}`. A valid non-enumerable supplied seat is silently ignored instead of changing that supplied field. Neither the patch type nor prose restricts supplied fields to enumerable-own properties. Original tests only supply literal patches. This witness uses an allowed patch field, not an extra id or ambiguous unknown-property policy.

Constructor explicitly reads id, label and optional disabled and constructs a fresh record. Its later spreads copy this internal literal. Hidden/inherited required values survive through ordinary reads; disabled is normalized to a boolean by the specified behavior. Original tests check field copies, ordering, enabled/disabled behavior and returned mutation isolation. No general descriptor/prototype preservation is required.

The contract defines a valid draft by the three enumerable own keys, with all three present. Reference only uses Object.keys to reject unknown keys, then reads required values without verifying their enumerable-own presence. A plain object with non-enumerable priority is accepted. This is not a demand to preserve arbitrary hidden extras: their exclusion is expressly permitted and the hidden-extra test is correct. It is failure to enforce the explicitly required key set.

`add` accepts primitive strings and creates a complete internal key/label literal; get/list spread only internal literals. menuConfig constructs its fixed keys explicitly. Tests verify detached results and exact menu keys. No public input record supplies descriptors or inherited fields.

Constructor reads every specified field directly and assigns primitives individually; toObject and parent construct fresh literals. Conditional parent spreads spread newly constructed literals, not the input. Required hidden/inherited values are not dropped, and unknown extras are expressly ignored. Tests verify returned-object isolation and optional parent presence. Direct runtime mutation of TypeScript-readonly instance properties is outside this property-copy adjudication; no new runtime-freezing claim is made.

Command fields type the marker/viewport/draw inputs; mutation/failure prose implies Result-returning recording transitions and submit explicitly returns count. Borrowed command observation is coherent. Completed, signaled submission is logically idle work for reset even though the private enum retains Submitted; a private phase name is not an external contradiction.

StartReply/Session fields and named string inputs support the constructor/completion API; observers are natural count/bool, completion/migration return the named errors. Tests do not impose an unrelated shape. Private u64 state exhaustion is not evidence of an executed API failure.

`try_read`/`try_write` boolean success, unit blocking acquisitions/unlocks and shared receivers are reasonably inferred from a manually unlocked gate expressly shareable through Arc. Destroy is explicitly typed. Bounded-yield scheduling-test risk is not an absent signature and is not converted into a failure here.

ReplicaId fixes ID type, borrowed `&str` lookup fixes stored digest semantics, and append/add failure prose supports Result. Reference u64 indices/counts are reasonable unsigned choices; original test explicitly exercises u64::MAX count without an incompatible alternative requirement. No generic numeric type or arbitrary-width interface was promised.

Missing(String) naturally carries the missing key and InvalidUnsigned/InvalidFlag(String) the invalid lexical value. These supplied payload-bearing error names, typed key access and value parsing make the reference/tests coherent; no contradictory error payload contract exists. The reference does not special-case a test input.

Public config/report are implementation-defined shapes with required command/options and `success`/messages behavior. Names and enums are inferable from the listed values. Tests use the natural report fields and deliberately do not demand exact diagnostic wording. Untested direct log/color retention is a coverage caveat, not missing types or a concrete incorrect output; reference retains both.

All formula operands are explicitly u32 and the prompt expressly requires saturating multiplication before division. Reference instead widens both operands to u64 before saturating, changing this operation's semantics. Small reachable witness and calculations below.

A valid failed withdrawal is promised to clear and restore its reservation, but record permits spending the restoration headroom while it is pending. The reference can then error on restoration and leave that reservation permanently pending until other state changes. Small public-call witness below; this is not private ID exhaustion.

The non-finite operand/result instruction is in the binary `either operand` promotion rule. The separate unary rule explicitly preserves exact variant/value. Reference rejects unary Plus(Float(INFINITY)), and the original final test requires that rejection, contradicting the unconditional unary identity rule. No need to invent mixed-kind/zero precedence.

Exact public CardLedger fields coexist with an express instruction to remember operation IDs internally and supplied constructors. The two-field presentation describes exposed fields, not a prohibition on private backing state, consistent with calibrated opaque sketches. Internal BTreeSet is justified by the prompt, not test accommodation. Competing malformed/duplicate errors do not establish a new precedence guarantee.

QuietSample::quiet() returning Self and iterator Item=Vec<T> are inferable from independent per-channel samples. Unsigned channel count/rate choices are reasonable; no fixed alternate widths are promised. Tests do not select width via conflicting typed arguments. Reference requires QuietSample only for iteration and supports non-Clone samples.

Named target pair and usize step arithmetic sufficiently specify the action representation; direction enum names and duration_ticks are explicit. Choosing u8 for the supplied1/2 durations is not an API contradiction. Large required output capacity is separate from missing field types; no extra full-domain execution claim.

Token{value,uses}, Data and Unauthorized are supplied in prose; ownership and string request results are reasonable. Optional borrowed cached-token observer and unsigned use count implement the described metadata. The named constructor/client errors are coherent choices; no contradictory hidden overload is added.

Three independent OutputLine generic parameters have independent associated Error types in the declared API. Reference adds R::Error=G::Error=B::Error and exposes all methods only under that extra condition. This excludes otherwise valid heterogeneous lines; neither the prompt nor the one-error-type tests authorize the restriction. The missing LineError payload schema must be fixed or the homogeneous restriction explicitly stated before admission.

Read `paused is optional; an absent value` as absence of that optional field, consistent with the following rule requiring a usable key/value in present fields. Therefore missing paused defaults false, while present paused= is InvalidPaused. Empty semicolon components are not granted an explicit ignore policy. These coherent choices do not establish test accommodation merely because another informal reading exists.

Fallible consuming stages naturally return Result<Self,PlanError>; build returns the named FeedPlan. The prompt requires both stages to have completed, not a new fetch after every subsequent for_user call, and does not prohibit repeated stages. Retaining already completed routes is thus not a demonstrated violation. No inferred invalidation or WrongOrder rule is imposed on repetition.

Macro punctuation is an implementation choice since no invocation syntax is frozen. A complete solution.rs used as a crate root puts SplatVector at the `$crate` path used by the exported macro; the original module harness reexports/imports that name to mirror the same layout. No independent submodule-packaging contract is promised. Positive count specifies the supported input domain; acceptance of zero outside that domain is not a required-rejection failure.

A canonical state codec reasonably rejects noncanonical decimal leading zeros; the task calls the encoding canonical and uses it for decoding, not merely a general number parser. No assertion demands accepting every decimal spelling. This differs from an explicit full-decimal-input contract. Existing normal forms and state invariant agree.

The function collects Text entries into a map; Group contributes descendants and an empty group contributes nothing. Interpret duplicate full paths as duplicate contributed map entries, not a separately promised uniqueness constraint on directory-node names. Reference rejects every duplicate Text output key, including descendants of repeated group names; duplicate empty groups create no map entry. No unsupported directory-identity validation is inferred.

Three comma fields `id,on:off,tag` have an invalid enabled field, not the wrong number of fields. Reference explicitly maps any colon there to WrongFieldCount, exactly matching the original special assertion, despite an InvalidEnabled variant and the declared comma-separated grammar. This is not merely priority between two simultaneously violated rules.

The required score scale is not fixed; the required observable preference is quicker wins/slower losses with smallest-amount ties and correct sign. Existing archived512-state independent oracle checks precisely optimal action under that preference plus sign for both turns. The code uses recursive negamax/bounds/table and returns actual table.len(). No extra exact-magnitude or table-layout contract is invented. This adjudication relies on existing executed coverage and does not claim a new exhaustive score/table-internals proof.

The prompt names MemberProfile and RegistrationResult but does not supply the profile identifier field or result union schema. The reference invents memberId and ok/profile/reason branches, and tests require them. These are not inferable merely from immutable locker registration. Exact error-message wording is not the basis: tests deliberately accept flexible messages. This is a self-contained API/clarity hold, not a claimed execution failure.

The prompt names RouteRecord and says every field is a string, but names only id/slug/title and never specifies the required path field. The reference reads, validates and returns path; tests reject numeric path and expect it round-tripped. Hold the missing required API field. The prior sparse malformed-record question need not decide this hold; no forced out-of-type sparse probe was run.

CaseRecord and Action are specified, but the other exported exact interfaces are not. Tests require RootState.import.inProgress, RemovalState.pendingId and DetailState.record while the prompt provides behavior rather than those field schemas. Hold missing public interface fields, not mutability of initialState: runtime freezing is not promised and unaffected branches explicitly retain identity.

The explicitly supported active update can be lost: a typed patch {active:false} remains a valid Partial<Pick<Account,...>> after Object.defineProperty(patch,"active",{enumerable:false}). Reference update reads displayName directly but merges active only through {...patch}, so a previously active account remains active. This is a static supported-property conflict, not an exotic extra-field requirement. Per-registration watch entries correctly implement independent duplicates and snapshots. Explicit-undefined optional-property policy is unnecessary to this finding.

CustomerSummary is requested without the id field/type or customer-validity rules. Reference requires string-or-finite-number id and tests use id; prose only establishes reference syntax/name trimming and invalid-customer rejection. Hold missing customer schema and validity domain. Do not hold a particular status discriminant spelling: tests accept alternatives.

Prompt gives Avatar an id and Vector2 position and assigns members to Arena. A supplied test instead executes a.members.push(a) on an Avatar. Reference adds unrequested Avatar.members to accommodate that access. A minimal implementation of the stated class API fails that test at TypeScript compilation. Static oracle/API accommodation; the codec identity algorithm itself is not declared broken.

The generation prompt requests three interfaces without naming or defining them and does not supply signIn parameter signatures. Reference invents CredentialsVerifier/TokenSink/SignInInput plus two overloads; tests require the four-argument object-verifier form. Hold missing API contract. The overload implementation is not itself alleged invalid.

Stricter plain-object validation implements the prose requirement rather than merely pleasing a Date-rejection test. Object.prototype and null prototypes are accepted. Call-side headers/params correctly override base entries, including undefined, and fresh map spreads preserve own __proto__ data. The specified nested maps are shallow maps; no arbitrary recursive value-cloning guarantee is inferred.

The prompt expressly requires elements to be exactly valid records shaped {sensor,value,sequence}; the exact-three-key validation has contract authority, including the extra-field rejection test. Inclusive upper bound, sequence order, copies and Map storage agree. This is not an unjustified test accommodation; no new execution or blanket descriptor-domain guarantee is claimed.

The reference require-nonempty helper rejects trim-empty strings for host IDs/names and workshop address, while prose requires nonempty strings and only specifies trimming for workshop-name uniqueness. An initial host {id:" ",name:"Host"} is nonempty under the stated ID rule but is statically rejected. This concrete domain narrowing independently holds the row; exact outer record-key closure need not be presumed from examples.

The supplied repair source accepts a null-prototype options object and checks its recognized fields; the correction newly requires Object.prototype exactly. Object.assign(Object.create(null),{insecure:true}) therefore changes from a supported source input to TypeError, rather than receiving the prescribed inverted Boolean. Prose says plain object but does not announce this null-prototype exclusion. Hold the repair-domain/clarity change, not the valid rejection of a custom inherited-prototype object in the test. Tests do not themselves demand null-prototype rejection.

Required text fields are described as nonempty strings; reference requireText instead rejects every whitespace-only string using trim(). A whitespace-only emblem is nonempty yet rejected. This is the same concrete nonempty-versus-nonblank domain narrowing as the calibrated sample. Do not base the hold on exact nested output-field spelling: the supplied substring assertions intentionally allow representational flexibility.

Emptiness is explicitly trim-based, but the entire contact email-pattern match is not specified as operating on trimmed input. Reference tests the trimmed contact, and the supplied test requires a space-padded email to pass even though whitespace prevents the raw entire string matching the stated pattern. Hold the normalization/test-contract ambiguity; do not silently transfer the emptiness normalization rule to the separate pattern rule.

Prompt explicitly asks for an async function. Tests require assert.throws(() => runStages(null)) synchronous validation; a true async function instead returns a rejected Promise. Reference accommodates this using an ordinary function with synchronous validation and an async inner function. Hold the incompatible async API/error contract; no runtime was needed to establish the language-level distinction.

Repeated registration of the same function is expressly idempotent. The Set is therefore the specified listener identity, not a missing per-call registration. Handles guard repeated invocation; removal and additions change only later snapshot notifications. No independent-generation handle ownership across unsubscribe/re-register cycles is promised. Do not import the distinct independent-registration criterion from other samples.

The contract specifies subscription order, snapshot membership and idempotent unsubscribe, but does not promise duplicate-function multiplicity or generation-isolated handles. Set registration preserves the order of present listeners; Array.from freezes membership; each handle has an idempotence guard. A first use of a still-unused duplicate handle removing the identity is not a stated violation. Optional initial?: DisplayDensity supports the normal omitted/undefined default convention, not an additional density error hold.

The supplied API already uses a Set; no instruction changes duplicate identity into independent registrations. Repair makes clear call set(null), preserving snapshots, immediate subscription delivery and idempotent handles. The snapshot promises which subscribers are called, not a frozen primitive across unspecified reentrant callbacks. No fresh duplicate/reentrancy requirement is imposed.

Arrays may contain holes, but no contract rule requires materializing holes as undefined values or rejecting sparse arrays. forEach visits present elements in index order and validates every returned formatter result. Empty input is explicitly handled; nonempty sparse arrays need not synthesize elements. Callback-driven input mutation shielding is also not promised. Close the speculative sparse policy question without asserting all conceivable array behaviors were tested.

Fresh full read resolves the earlier broad-alias caveat using the specific contract: LOAD_OK and selector explicitly require shallow copies, and RESET explicitly returns the initial object. The no-alias instruction is read consistently as a fresh handled root except for its express RESET exception, not an unannounced deep clone of all shared state. Do not silently claim a deep-alias proof; the concrete previously named RESET contradiction is discharged by its explicit rule.

Required own-string-key preservation is broader than own-enumerable value validation. A plain registry with non-enumerable own x=0 and enumerable y=1 passes validation; toggling y spreads away x, contrary to the same-own-string-key requirement. This does not depend on allowing an invalid selected value. Source: JS_TS_RESIDUAL_REVIEW_12.md retained this descriptor question; fresh full read now provides the concrete loss.

A valid externally supplied normalized state can have a null-prototype byId dictionary with a non-enumerable engine entry and enumerable wing entry, and order ["engine","wing"]. PIN_PART wing copies with Object.assign, dropping engine instead of preserving the unaffected record and normalized contents. No own-enumerable dictionary restriction is stated. Hold that required-entry loss; arbitrary extra part-field preservation is not needed. Source: JS_TS_RESIDUAL_REVIEW_25.md.

The prompt distinguishes non-integers (TypeError) from out-of-range integers (RangeError), yet reference and supplied test require TypeError for pageCount=Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1. That value is an integer outside the permitted safe range. The exception-class contract and oracle conflict statically. Do not additionally claim an actually exercised refresh-counter exhaustion. Source: JS_TS_RESIDUAL_REVIEW_29.md.

Fresh full prompt/source/reference/tests explicitly say registers once by identity; Set deduplication is correct. Idempotence guards repeated calls to each handle, not an unstated independent registration generation. Snapshot array plus per-call id/oldId also preserves the explicitly allowed reentrant transition arguments. Callback exception recovery is not specified. The old duplicate-lifecycle/error-handling caveat does not justify a new hold. Source: JS_TS_RESIDUAL_REVIEW_29.md.
